Subject: Realtime stream intermittently stalling this morning

Hi Sofia,

We started seeing intermittent stalls in our live assistant this morning around 08:55 PST. The client receives partial chunks and then the stream pauses for ~3-8s before resuming. This is impacting our real-time UX — users are seeing stutters and truncated replies.

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick report and the attachments. We’re digging in now. Initial notes and immediate customer-side mitigations you can apply while we triage: 

Immediate mitigations (client-side, low-friction):
- Reduce the streaming max_tokens window to 256 for live endpoints; this reduces the amount of in-flight token state and lowers backpressure risk.
- Increase the client-side socket read timeout to 12s (from default 5s) and surface a subtle loading indicator — this prevents premature client disconnects during transient stalls.
- If possible, switch to a non-streaming completion for critical UX paths (single request, non-stream) as a temporary fallback during peak windows.
- Send a short heartbeat (lightweight ping) every 4s from the client to keep intermediate network middleboxes from idling connections.

We’ve ingested your diagnostic IDs and a PCAP sample; we’ll correlate with our edge telemetry. Can you confirm the session IDs in diagnostic-ids.txt and whether the issue is reproducible on replay? If you can share one full request/response pair with timestamps, that will speed things up.

I’ll loop in our on-call infra and streaming teams now and follow up within 2 hours with root-cause hypotheses and a mitigation plan.

Best,

Folks — forwarding BrightPay’s report. Repro around 08:55 PST. Customer saw partial chunks then 3–8s pauses; no 5xxs.

What we’ve pulled so far (preliminary):
- Edge node token-queue depth increased on a subset of hosts serving the us-west region during their traffic spike; KV cache misses spiked concurrently which increased CPU scheduling for tokenization and GC work.
- Streaming runtime observed burst scheduling that delayed token flushes to the network stack for short windows (~200–600ms), which accumulated into multi-second pauses at the client when combined with middlebox buffering.

Immediate infra steps I recommend before we finish root cause:
1) Apply a short-lived kernel net.core.rmem_max bump on affected host group to reduce kernel-level TCP buffer pressure (rolling, 5m window).
2) Force KV cache warmup on the shard pool serving BrightPay traffic (evict stale entries and re-populate) — avoids the cold-miss CPU penalty.
3) Temporarily increase max worker threads for streaming runtime on the node pool to reduce scheduling delays (rollback after 2h).

Attachments included from customer and our collect: diagnostic-ids.txt, pcap-sample-stub.pcap. I’ve uploaded full traces to Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/brightpay-token-diagnostics (internal).

Let me know if you want me to open an SLA exception for extra account support. I’ll also request short-term quota bump for the Dedicated pool serving them if we need headroom.

— Sofia

Subject: Update: BrightPay streaming stalls — cause, mitigations, and next steps

Hi Alex — quick update and summary of actions. Thank you again for the diagnostic bundle and patience while we investigated.

Root cause (summary):
- During BrightPay’s peak on 29 Nov we observed a traffic spike that empty-hit our preferred shard set and caused a transient increase in KV cache misses. Those misses led to CPU scheduling spikes inside the tokenization path on a subset (~12%) of edge hosts.
- The streaming runtime’s scheduling behavior combined with client-side buffering in certain middleboxes produced partial chunk delivery followed by accumulated pause windows of 3–8s. Importantly: requests did not error, they were delayed.

What we changed (actions taken by Redwood):
- Applied a rolling kernel TCP buffer tuning and a short worker-thread increase on the affected node group (rolled back 2 hours after stabilization).
- Forced KV cache re-population on the shard pool; we adjusted cache eviction heuristics to reduce cold-miss probability for short traffic surges.
- Deployed a small streaming runtime patch to ensure token flush prioritization when IO queues exceed target depth (hotfix rolled to us-west pool).
- Added an automated early-detection alert for token-queue depth so we can proactively scale or drain before client-visible stalls.

Customer-facing mitigations we recommend (recap):
- Set streaming max_tokens to 256 for peak windows.
- Increase client socket read timeout to 12s and implement a non-streaming fallback for critical flows.
- Add a client heartbeat/ping every 4s to keep intermediate network devices from idling connections.

Next steps and asks from BrightPay:
- Please confirm whether you want Redwood to open an SLA exception for additional support time this month (I can submit the request; see attached SLA request).
- If you can replay one full request/response trace (UTC timestamps) where you saw the 3–8s pause, we’ll correlate against the node-level traces for a final verification step.

Attachments: sla-exception-request.pdf (internal request form).
